name: Phat Diem stone church
kicker: Stone and wood at Kim Sơn
summary: Give a morning to Kim Sơn’s stone-and-wood church, built from 1875 to 1898 by Đức cha Phê rô Trần Lục. The complex is in xã Lưu Phương, a ride out from the karst valley. The wooden nave is given as both 52 columns and 16 columns. It became a national relic in 1987.
dotReason: The Kim Sơn church, a separate ground from the karst

heroCaption: The stone front and the wooden nave at Phát Diệm
body: The complex went up from 1875 to 1898. The tourism page names Đức cha Phê rô Trần Lục, and it places Kim Sơn’s reclamation with Nguyễn Công Trứ in 1829. Buildings it names include the phương đình, nhà thờ Lớn, the chapels of Phê rô, Giu-se, and Rô Cô, and a grotto. Phương Đình is three stone storeys. The page says Điện Trái tim Đức mẹ, also called nhà thờ đá, is stone from the floor to the roof. Nhà thờ Lớn is wood: six rows of lim columns, and the same paragraph prints both 52 columns and 16 columns. Keep both counts. It became a national relic in 1987.

The hero is the stone chapel front, the cross, and the wooden nave beside it. Commons calls that frame Saint Peter’s Chapel. The file name is the complex. Both wordings stay. A street number was not on the tourism page. The support phone is 02293.862.058. A fee and a mass hour were not printed. Check on arrival.
